Method of Attack: Deletes Shadow Volume Copies using vssadmin.exe
Terminates specific processes and Windows services
Encrypts files except excluded folders and files
Demands million-dollar ransom to not leak data and release decryptor
Creates ransom note with TOR negotiation site link
Threat actors steal data and threaten to publish if ransom not paid
Impacted Systems: Devices with folders such as C:\msocache, C:\$windows.~ws, C:\system volume information, C:\perflogs, C:\programdata, C:\program files (x86), C:\program files, C:\$windows.~bt, C:\windows, C:\windows.old, C:\boot
Systems running processes like sql.exe, oracle.exe, firefox.exe, outlook.exe, winword.exe, steam.exe, etc.
Systems running services like vss, sql, sophos, veeam, backup, vmms
Indicators of Compromise: Use of cmd.com /c vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet
Screenshot of accessed file system as proof of breach
TOR negotiation site link in ransom note
